w: Two blocks of sandstone wilderness totalling 93.5 square kilometres, tucked into the Elbe Sandstone Mountains near Dresden. The park picks up exactly where its Czech twin, Bohemian Switzerland National Park, ends at the border, so gorges and table hills read as one unbroken range.
s: Where sandstone wilderness meets its Czech twin
_facts: 93.5 sq km across two sections
adjoins Bohemian Switzerland National Park across the Czech border
sits in the German part of the Elbe Sandstone Mountains near Dresden

w: A jagged table hill split into three crown-shaped points, each one climbable, above the village of Schona. Two lions were carved into the rock at its southern end by unknown artists. Caspar David Friedrich sketched this outcrop, later reworked into his painting Wanderer above the Sea of Fog.
s: The rock sketched into Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
_facts: three crown-like sandstone points, each climbable
two lions carved into the rock by unknown artists
sketched by Caspar David Friedrich, later reused as the undercoat for Wanderer above the Sea of Fog

w: A modest sandstone arch barely 2.3 metres high, standing on the red-marked E3 path between Mezni Louka and Vysoka Lipa in Bohemian Switzerland. Its name means Little Pravcice Gate, borrowed from its far larger neighbour, the Pravcicka brana, Europe's biggest natural sandstone arch.
s: Little sibling of Europe's biggest sandstone arch
_facts: sandstone arch about 2.3m high and 3.3m wide
on the E3 long-distance path between Mezni Louka and Vysoka Lipa
named after the larger Pravcicka brana, the biggest natural sandstone arch in Europe

w: A 533-metre basalt cone rising oddly out of a range otherwise carved from sandstone, on the old road south of Doubice toward Chribska. Locals call it Spravedlnost, roughly Justice, and it comes wrapped in old legend the record no longer spells out.
s: A basalt cone wrapped in legend, not sandstone
_facts: 533m volcanic basalt cone amid a sandstone range
shrouded in local legend under its German name, Iricht
local mountain of the village of Doubice, above Nova Doubice

w: Twin sandstone tables about 7km south of Bad Schandau: the Grosser Zschirnstein, at 561m the highest hill in Saxon Switzerland, and its smaller neighbour the Kleiner Zschirnstein at 473m. Both rise from forest and can be climbed on foot for wide views across Saxon-Bohemian Switzerland.
s: Twin table hills, the tallest in Saxon Switzerland
_facts: two table hills: Grosser Zschirnstein (561m) and Kleiner Zschirnstein (473m)
Grosser Zschirnstein is the highest hill in Saxon Switzerland
both climbable on foot; Panoramahotel Wolfsberg is the usual base

w: A 15th-century hilltop castle turned prison: during the Second World War, Burg Hohnstein held Allied officers as the POW camp Oflag IV-A. Centuries of fortress walls repurposed for barbed wire and roll calls, in the middle of the sandstone hiking country that now draws walkers past its ramparts instead of guards.
s: A 15th-century castle turned WWII officers' camp
_facts: 15th-century castle in the town of Hohnstein, Saxon Switzerland
used in WWII as Oflag IV-A, a German POW camp for Allied officers

w: A ruined rock castle cut into sandstone above Doubice, once known as Karlstejn before it fell into ruin and picked up the nickname Wustes Schloss, the Waste Castle. Little survives beyond rock-cut chambers and footings, in a corner of Bohemian Switzerland long fortified against its own cliffs.
s: A rock castle nicknamed the Waste Castle
_facts: ruined rock castle in Doubice, Czech Republic
older name Karlstejn, also called Unterer Karlstein or Wustes Schloss (Waste Castle)
carved into the Elbe Sandstone Mountains

w: Saxon Switzerland's word for fire, earned from wildfires that once burned through the forest below. A log cabin went up here in 1856, rebuilt in stone in 1877, and the resulting Brand-Baude, modernised in 2007, still marks one of the region's most famous viewpoints on the Malerweg trail.
s: The viewpoint on the Painters' Way trail
_facts: one of Saxon Switzerland's most famous viewpoints, above the river Polenz
name means fire, after past wildfires in the surrounding forest
1856 log cabin rebuilt in stone in 1877, now the Brand-Baude visitor centre
a stop on the Malerweg (Painters' Way) hiking trail

w: Built in 1883, this 25-metre lattice tower on Goetzinger's Height predates the Eiffel Tower and ranks among the oldest lattice towers standing anywhere. Renovated in 1992, it still gives a clear sweep over the Elbe Sandstone Mountains, the Ore Mountains and the Lusatian Highlands.
s: A lattice tower older than the Eiffel Tower
_facts: 25m lattice observation tower built 1883, near Neustadt in Sachsen
predates the Eiffel Tower; one of the oldest lattice towers in the world
renovated 1992; view over the Elbe Sandstone Mountains, Ore Mountains and Lusatian Highlands
adjoining inn reopened 1 April 2006 after years closed

w: A 130-metre sandstone tower on the Grosser Winterberg's northern slopes, nicknamed Vorderes Raubschloss, the Robbers' Castle. The Barony of Wildenstein once kept a watchtower on top, part of a chain of lookouts through the Affensteine rocks. No masonry survives, but climbers still queue for the summit.
s: A sandstone tower nicknamed the Robbers' Castle
_facts: about 130m-high rock formation, also called Vorderes Raubschloss
once carried a watchtower for the Barony of Wildenstein
on the northern slopes of the Grosser Winterberg, in the Affensteine rocks
today a popular climbing peak
